pillars.title: Demand Runway
pillars.claim: The biggest cloud companies keep raising AI spending into next year, so demand is set by their budgets rather than a cycle turning.
why: The four US hyperscalers, Oracle and the GPU clouds are the biggest buyers.
Their capex plans decide how many racks get built next year.
Custom chips at those same buyers are the main thing that could take share.
pillars.killCriteria: Two of the four largest US cloud companies cut their next-year capex plans.
pillars.statusReason: None of the big four is cutting, and three plan to spend more in 2027. The catch is custom chips: more of that money goes to TPUs and Trainium, so it no longer turns into NVIDIA orders one for one.
pillars.nextCheck: AWS re:Invent (Nov 30 to Dec 4), then the big four's Q4 calls in late January.

pillars.title: Supply Limit
pillars.claim: Shipments are capped by TSMC's packaging and HBM supply rather than by orders, which keeps pricing firm.
why: TSMC makes the chips and packages them with CoWoS.
SK hynix, Samsung and Micron supply the HBM memory.
Foxconn, Quanta and Wistron assemble the systems.
pillars.killCriteria: NVIDIA guides gross margin below 70% for two quarters in a row.
pillars.statusReason: Margins are guided to 71-72%, one to two points above the line, and management calls that the bottom. Demand still beats supply, but memory makers now set the price, so the cushion is thin.
pillars.nextCheck: Micron's results on Dec 17, then NVIDIA's Q4 report in late February.

pillars.title: KPIs
pillars.claim: The numbers management leads with, and the outside data that moves before they're reported.

kpis.latest: $107.6B in the October quarter, up 110% from a year ago

kpis.expected: 71-72% guided for Q4, which management calls the bottom; 72-73% next year
kpis.read: HBM prices are set to more than double in 2027, which is why the guide dips. NVIDIA's own price increases are the offset.

pillars.statusReason: The early data says growth is still accelerating, with record supplier sales and rising GPU rental prices. Margins are the soft spot: memory costs pull the next quarter down before NVIDIA's own price increases kick in.
pillars.nextCheck: TSMC's November sales on Dec 10 and Micron's results on Dec 17.

nodes.summary: SAMR's preliminary finding in September 2025 left a fine of 1% to 10% of prior-year China sales, or remedies, hanging over NVIDIA.
brief: China's market regulator
An open Mellanox case gives Beijing a lever to fine NVIDIA or restrict its networking sales.
nodes.health: Preliminary violation found September 2025; no final penalty announced as of November 2026.

nodes.label: US Justice Department
nodes.relation: Reviewing the $11.9 billion Hugging Face deal inside a wider look at NVIDIA's practices
nodes.summary: The antitrust division is reviewing NVIDIA's deals, including Hugging Face and the Groq licensing arrangement.
brief: US antitrust enforcer
A broad conduct case could limit bundling that keeps NVIDIA's pricing and margins firm.
nodes.health: No second request or lawsuit publicly reported as of late October 2026.

nodes.label: European Commission
nodes.relation: Informal antitrust investigation into NVIDIA's data center business
nodes.summary: The Commission has been asking the industry how to define data center products, the groundwork for a bundling or dominance case.
brief: EU competition authority
An EU case could force NVIDIA to unbundle networking from GPUs in European sales.
nodes.health: Took new steps in its informal NVIDIA probe in October 2026.

nodes.label: Megaspeed
nodes.relation: Singapore cloud buyer of NVIDIA chips suspected of diverting them to China
nodes.summary: Megaspeed bought more than $4 billion of NVIDIA chips, and Treasury wants it blacklisted.
brief: Southeast Asian GPU cloud operator
It is the case Washington is using to tighten sales into Southeast Asia.
nodes.health: Bought over $4 billion of NVIDIA chips; Treasury wants it blacklisted.

nodes.label: Taiwan Strait
nodes.relation: Military risk to TSMC, which makes and packages nearly all NVIDIA chips
nodes.summary: China ran an unannounced, multi-fleet exercise around Taiwan in early November that analysts read as practice for isolating the island.
brief: Geopolitical risk to chip supply
Any blockade would cut the TSMC wafers and CoWoS packaging NVIDIA depends on.
nodes.health: About 100 Chinese ships deployed in early November; no blockade followed.

nodes.label: Vanguard
nodes.relation: Largest institutional holder of NVIDIA common stock
nodes.summary: Vanguard reported 1.78 billion NVIDIA shares, 7.31% of the class, in its Schedule 13G for March 31, 2026.
brief: Largest index fund holder
Passive ownership this large steadies the register but cannot vote out a governance problem.
nodes.health: Owned 7.31% of NVIDIA, 1,777,408,252 shares, at March 31, 2026.

nodes.label: Mark Stevens
nodes.relation: NVIDIA director and one of its largest individual holders
nodes.summary: Stevens sold about $298 million of stock in September at around $220, well above where the shares trade now.
brief: NVIDIA board director
A director selling this much near the top is a read on insider conviction.
nodes.health: Still holds about 27.5 million shares directly and through trusts after the sale.

nodes.label: AMD
nodes.relation: Sells MI450 GPUs in Helios racks against NVIDIA's rack-scale systems
nodes.summary: AMD is the only merchant GPU rival shipping full racks, and its MI450 launch put Helios into the same five big buyers NVIDIA depends on.
brief: Merchant GPU and rack rival
Every Helios rack AMD ships to a hyperscaler is a rack NVIDIA did not sell.
nodes.health: Data center revenue a record $8.5B, up 97%; Q4 guide about $17B.

nodes.label: Broadcom
nodes.relation: Designs custom XPUs for Google, Meta, OpenAI and Anthropic, and sells Ethernet switches that compete with NVLink and Spectrum-X
nodes.summary: Broadcom is the biggest builder of custom AI chips for NVIDIA's own customers and is pushing open Ethernet into the scale-up network NVLink owns today.
brief: Custom AI chip and switch maker
Its XPU wins are the clearest measure of how much hyperscaler spend skips NVIDIA.
nodes.health: AI chip revenue $16.7B last quarter, up 221%; guiding $21.7B next quarter.

nodes.label: Arista Networks
nodes.relation: Sells Ethernet AI switches built on Broadcom silicon against NVIDIA Spectrum-X and InfiniBand
nodes.summary: Arista is the main switch vendor competing with NVIDIA's networking business inside AI clusters, mostly on Broadcom chips.
brief: Ethernet AI switch vendor
Arista's wins cap how much of each AI cluster's network NVIDIA captures.
nodes.health: Q3 2026 revenue $3.66B, up 58.5%, its fastest growth as a public company.

nodes.label: Huawei
nodes.relation: Sells Ascend accelerators and Atlas superclusters to Chinese AI developers in place of NVIDIA GPUs
nodes.summary: Huawei is taking the China market that export rules closed to NVIDIA, though its output is capped by domestic manufacturing.
brief: China's leading AI accelerator maker
Huawei's share gains make NVIDIA's lost China revenue harder to win back.
nodes.health: Shipped 572,000 AI accelerators in China in H1 2026, a 28% share.

nodes.label: Samsung Electronics
nodes.relation: HBM4 supplier; reported: about 30% of Vera Rubin HBM4 volume
nodes.summary: Samsung is NVIDIA's second HBM4 source, which matters for both volume and bargaining leverage against SK hynix.
brief: Second HBM4 memory supplier
A working second HBM4 source gives NVIDIA more volume and some leverage on memory prices.
nodes.health: Q3 operating profit hit a record KRW 107.4 trillion, KRW 106.5 trillion from chips.

nodes.label: SPIL
nodes.relation: Advanced packaging and optical-engine partner under a multiyear NVIDIA agreement
nodes.summary: SPIL, part of ASE, is NVIDIA's main packaging capacity outside TSMC, now backed by NVIDIA money.
brief: Advanced packaging second source
SPIL adds packaging capacity outside TSMC, which loosens the tightest bottleneck on NVIDIA's shipments.
nodes.health: Backed by multibillion-dollar NVIDIA funding, with dedicated capacity rising through mid-2029.

nodes.label: Amkor Technology
nodes.relation: Packaging partner with multiyear NVIDIA agreements covering Arizona and South Korea
nodes.summary: Amkor is building packaging capacity in Arizona and Korea, partly funded by NVIDIA, as a second path beyond TSMC.
brief: Packaging and interposer supplier
Amkor gives NVIDIA packaging outside Taiwan, cutting both the bottleneck and the geography risk.
nodes.health: Holds nearly $3 billion of NVIDIA agreements, including prepayments, for Arizona and Korea.

nodes.label: IBIDEN
nodes.relation: Supplies the ABF substrates NVIDIA GPUs are mounted on
nodes.summary: IBIDEN is NVIDIA's main substrate maker, and substrates are now one of the named limits on how many GPUs ship.
brief: GPU package substrate maker
Substrates are a named shipment constraint, and new IBIDEN capacity does not arrive until 2028.
nodes.health: Ono plant is expanding to three times current capacity, ramping from Q1 2028.

nodes.label: King Yuan Electronics
nodes.relation: Tests NVIDIA chips; building US test sites on an NVIDIA advance payment
nodes.summary: KYEC does final testing on NVIDIA chips, and testing has become another capacity limit NVIDIA is paying to remove.
brief: Chip testing services provider
NVIDIA is prepaying KYEC so testing does not cap shipments as volumes double.
nodes.health: A $1.1 billion NVIDIA advance funds US test sites, with volume production from April 2027.

nodes.label: Kinsus
nodes.relation: ABF substrate maker under a new NVIDIA capacity deal
nodes.summary: Kinsus makes the ABF substrates that every GPU package sits on, a material that has been short all year.
brief: ABF chip substrate maker
Substrates are a hidden cap on GPU output, and NVIDIA is paying to lift it.
nodes.health: Expanding NVIDIA-dedicated ABF capacity more than 3.5x, with full output by Q3 2028.

nodes.label: Intel
nodes.relation: EMIB packaging offered as a cheaper second source to CoWoS
nodes.summary: Intel's EMIB packaging gives custom-chip buyers like Google a way around TSMC's sold-out CoWoS lines.
brief: Rival packaging second source
Cheaper non-TSMC packaging lets custom chips grow without waiting behind NVIDIA.
nodes.health: Its foundry unit lost $10.3 billion on $17.8 billion of revenue in 2025.

nodes.label: US grid equipment shortage
nodes.relation: Transformer and turbine lead times gate when data centers can switch on
nodes.summary: Transformers, switchgear and gas turbines for new data centers now take years to arrive, which can delay rack deployments.
brief: Power equipment bottleneck
If buildings cannot get power, customers slow GPU orders regardless of budget.
nodes.health: Large power transformers now take more than three years to deliver.

signals.headline: NVIDIA's data center revenue hit $107.6B in the October quarter, up 110% from a year ago
signals.whyItMatters: This is the KPI itself: data center revenue was $107.6B in the quarter ended October 25, up 110% from a year ago and 21% from the prior quarter, though growth eased from 117% in the July quarter.
signals.evidence: Data Center: Third-quarter revenue was $107.6 billion, up 21% from the previous quarter and up 110% from a year ago.

signals.headline: Can AI Infrastructure Demand Sustain NVIDIA's Q3 Data Center Growth?
signals.whyItMatters: Analysts expected $101.24B of data center revenue and NVIDIA reported $107.6B, a beat of about 6%, so the street was still too low going into the quarter.
signals.evidence: The Zacks Consensus Estimate for third-quarter data center revenues is pegged at $101.24 billion

signals.headline: Earnings Watch | NVIDIA Q3 FY27
signals.whyItMatters: The street had $124.8B of total revenue pencilled in for the January quarter and NVIDIA guided $130B, so next quarter's estimates have to move up.
signals.evidence: Consensus revenue for the January quarter (Q4 FY27) is $124.8 billion.

signals.headline: NVIDIA Q3 Earnings Beat on Data Center Demand & Rubin Ramp-Up
signals.whyItMatters: Part of the $130B guide is calendar, not demand: the January quarter has an extra week, and receivables days rose to 64 from 60 on longer payment terms for some customers.
signals.evidence: The outlook includes an additional week and assumes no Data Center compute revenues from China.

signals.headline: TSMC October 2026 Revenue Report
signals.whyItMatters: TSMC's record October means more NVIDIA chips are being made and packaged, which shows up in NVIDIA's data center revenue over the next one to two quarters.
signals.evidence: revenue for October 2026 was approximately NT$586.89 billion, an increase of 14.7 percent from September 2026

signals.headline: Hon Hai's revenue hits record NT$1.3 trillion in October
signals.whyItMatters: Total sales hit a record, but the cloud segment that carries NVIDIA racks slipped from September on supply limits, so the first month of NVIDIA's January quarter was not a straight line up.
signals.evidence: recorded a slight decline from September despite continued strong demand for artificial intelligence (AI) applications

signals.headline: Quanta (2382) October consolidated revenue NT$353.25 billion, up 104.0% year on year
signals.whyItMatters: Quanta's sales doubled from a year ago and rose 8.6% from September, which points to NVIDIA rack shipments still climbing at the start of NVIDIA's January quarter.
signals.evidence: 10 月合併營收 3,532.50 億元，較上（9）月成長 8.6%，與去年同期相比為年增 104.0%

signals.headline: Quanta (2382): fewer AI racks shipped, revenue still grows as average price takes over
signals.whyItMatters: Quanta shipped slightly fewer AI racks in the September quarter and expects fewer again in December, so growth is coming from higher prices per rack rather than more units, a weaker base if pricing stalls.
signals.evidence: 公司預期第 4 季方向相同：出貨總櫃數比第 3 季略減，營收繼續季增。

signals.headline: Wistron (3231) October revenue NT$402.6 billion, up 117.6% year on year
signals.whyItMatters: Wistron makes NVIDIA's GPU baseboards, so sales more than doubling and rising 5.7% from September point to steady GPU volumes into NVIDIA's January quarter.
signals.evidence: 10 月營收，達 4,026.15 億元，較 9 月成長 5.7%，較去年同期成長 117.6%

signals.headline: Wiwynn (6669) October revenue NT$165.13 billion, up 80.9% year on year
signals.whyItMatters: Hyperscaler server builds are still up 80.9% on last year, but sales fell 4.3% from September, and part of this spending goes to racks built on the clouds' own chips instead of NVIDIA's.
signals.evidence: 10 月營收，達 1,651.32 億元，較 9 月成長 -4.3%，較去年同期成長 80.9%

signals.headline: Alphabet's Q3 2026 results: search and cloud grow, free cash flow is negative
signals.whyItMatters: Alphabet spent $51.4B in the quarter and says 2027 capex will rise significantly, which funds next year's hyperscale data center orders, though some of it builds TPU systems that compete with NVIDIA.
signals.evidence: $51.4 billion in capital expenditures, or CapEx

signals.headline: Microsoft's stock rises on solid earnings and revenue beat, with Azure growing 48%
signals.whyItMatters: Microsoft spent $45.2B against estimates as high as $50.67B because some third-party capacity arrived late, a reminder that data center build delays can push NVIDIA shipments out a quarter.
signals.evidence: Microsoft spent $45.2 billion on capital expenditures and finance leases, up by around 30% from a year before.

signals.headline: CSP CapEx Projected to Exceed US$1.5 Trillion in 2027, with AI Server Revenue Growing Over 90% YoY on Higher Shipments and Prices, Says TrendForce
signals.whyItMatters: If the nine largest clouds lift capex 60% to over $1.5 trillion and AI server revenue grows over 90% in 2027, NVIDIA's data center revenue has room to keep growing next year.
signals.evidence: In 2027, this figure is expected to surpass $1.5 trillion, representing a further 60% YoY increase.

signals.headline: Ornn Exchange data shows GPU rental prices climbing month-on-month across chip generations
signals.whyItMatters: Blackwell rents up 32% and H200 rents up 49% in a month mean GPU clouds can earn more per chip, which is what makes them place the next NVIDIA order.
signals.evidence: the B200, part of Nvidia's Blackwell line, was renting for approximately $9.84 per GPU-hour. That reading was up 32% from the preceding month.

signals.headline: NVIDIA Q3 FY27 gross margin 74.8% versus 74.03% expected
signals.whyItMatters: Beating the margin bar by almost a point shows memory costs have not yet outrun NVIDIA's pricing.
signals.evidence: Gross margin 74.8% vs. 74.03% expected

signals.headline: HBM Supply Constraints Persist, 2027 Price Outlook Revised Upward with Blended ASP Forecast to Rise 121% YoY, Says TrendForce
signals.whyItMatters: HBM more than doubling in price is the main reason NVIDIA's margin steps down, and the FY28 recovery depends on passing it on.
signals.evidence: Blended ASP is now projected to jump 121% YoY.

signals.headline: AI Server Demand Sustains Memory Contract Price Increases in 4Q26, While Consumer-Side Pressure Persists, Says TrendForce
signals.whyItMatters: Another 10-15% rise in conventional DRAM lands in the quarter NVIDIA already guided as its margin low.
signals.evidence: Conventional DRAM contract prices are projected to grow 10–15% QoQ in 4Q26

signals.headline: SK hynix says DRAM and HBM booked through 2029 as profit soars to $62 billion
signals.whyItMatters: A supplier earning about 80% operating margin with volumes sold out to 2029 holds the pricing power, which caps how far NVIDIA's margin can recover.
signals.evidence: our DRAM and HBM volumes for the next three years through 2029 are effectively sold out

signals.headline: TSMC Reportedly Eyes 20% CoWoS Price Hike, Skips Equipment Price Renegotiations Amid AI Demand Surge
signals.whyItMatters: Packaging and wafer hikes in 2027 stack on top of memory, so NVIDIA's own price increases have to cover two cost pushes.
signals.evidence: weighing price hikes of up to 20%

signals.headline: AI back-end network switch sales surpass front-end networks for the first time in 2Q26
signals.whyItMatters: The AI switch market is growing fast, but white-box Celestica still leads and Cisco is gaining, so Spectrum-X share is not guaranteed.
signals.evidence: Celestica retained the leading position, followed closely by NVIDIA

signals.headline: Ethernet Switch Market Surges 43.4% to $18.9B in 2Q26 as AI Infrastructure Demand Drives Record Datacenter Spending
signals.whyItMatters: Spectrum-X nearly tripled its Ethernet sales on last year, though its share slipped from 21.5% to 20.4%, so the growth is the market as much as share gains.
signals.evidence: NVIDIA $2.5B, 20.4% share, up 181.1% year over year

signals.headline: LandMark October revenue NT$570 million, up 183% year on year
signals.whyItMatters: Laser epiwafer sales still rising in October point to optics demand holding into NVIDIA's January quarter.
signals.evidence: 10 月營收,達 5.70 億元,較去年同期成長 183.0%

signals.headline: Innolight third-quarter profit up 174% as 1.6T shipments ramp
signals.whyItMatters: Optics revenue nearly tripling with 1.6T accelerating matches the networking surge NVIDIA reported three weeks later.
signals.evidence: 1.6T產品收入成長加快; revenue 人民幣278億元, up 172% YoY

signals.headline: Microsoft sees $170bn capex in fiscal 2027 but says it will stay cash flow positive
signals.whyItMatters: The largest buyer is raising its budget again and can fund it from cash, which supports next year's rack orders.
signals.evidence: expects to stay free cash flow positive this fiscal year

signals.headline: Google misses revenue expectations, Alphabet stock sinks in early after-hours trading
signals.whyItMatters: Alphabet promised a significant capex increase for 2027 even as the stock fell, so a second of the big four is still raising spend.
signals.evidence: continues to expect its capital expenditures to "increase significantly" in 2027

signals.headline: Alphabet's Q3 2026 results: search and cloud grow, free cash flow is negative
signals.whyItMatters: Google is now building inventory to sell TPU systems to others, which turns a buyer into a direct competitor for the same budgets.
signals.evidence: a buildup of inventory for TPU-system sales

signals.headline: AWS grows 39% and Amazon will spend even more on AI in 2027
signals.whyItMatters: A third hyperscaler says 2027 spend goes up, which makes the kill criterion of two cuts look far away.
signals.evidence: expects to spend "meaningfully more" in 2027

signals.headline: Meta Platforms posts negative free cash flow for the first time since 2012
signals.whyItMatters: Meta is still spending hard on NVIDIA gear, but it is now funding that from its balance sheet rather than cash flow.
signals.evidence: This hasn't happened since 2012

signals.headline: Oracle announces Q1 results driven by triple digit growth in cloud infrastructure revenues
signals.whyItMatters: A $664 billion backlog means many more NVIDIA clusters, but Oracle is paying for them with negative cash flow and a $20 billion share sale.
signals.evidence: RPO up $209 billion year-over-year to $664 billion

signals.headline: Oracle sends force majeure notice on its New Mexico Stargate data center
signals.whyItMatters: If the 2.45GW Jupiter campus slips past 2028 because of power delays, the NVIDIA racks meant for it slip too.
signals.evidence: February 1, 2027

signals.headline: CoreWeave: record Q3 revenue reaches $3.66 billion as backlog grows to $132.5 billion
signals.whyItMatters: A growing backlog at a pure NVIDIA cloud turns almost one for one into GPU and networking orders.
signals.evidence: 2026 capital expenditures of $37 billion to $39 billion

signals.headline: OpenAI posts steep losses even as quarterly revenue rises to $10 billion, WSJ reports
signals.whyItMatters: Revenue is growing fast, but OpenAI still loses more than it books, and Oracle and CoreWeave orders depend on it paying.
signals.evidence: operating losses widened to $10.9 billion from $10.1 billion

signals.headline: OpenAI's compute plan rises to $856bn while its projected cash burn improves
signals.whyItMatters: OpenAI's compute plan is far bigger than its cash, so a weak funding round in 2027 or 2028 would hit NVIDIA demand through several clouds at once.
signals.evidence: on track to exhaust that by 2028

signals.headline: NVIDIA's Q3 filing shows up to $118 billion of credit guarantees, mostly for OpenAI's Ohio campus
signals.whyItMatters: NVIDIA is now providing credit support for a buyer's land, power and buildings, so part of its demand is propped up by its own balance sheet and an OpenAI default would land on NVIDIA.
signals.evidence: up to $105 billion supports guarantees for SB Energy's data center project in Ohio

signals.headline: Anthropic details long-term compute commitments in amended IPO filing
signals.whyItMatters: The fastest-growing lab is reserving its biggest new compute on Google TPUs, so that spend goes to a rival chip rather than NVIDIA.
signals.evidence: $125 billion to $150 billion for additional Google TPU compute

signals.headline: Saudi Arabia's Humain expands Nvidia deal with 84MW AI computing plan
signals.whyItMatters: Sovereign buyers add demand that does not depend on hyperscaler budgets, although this deal is small and not yet final.
signals.evidence: develop up to 84 megawatts of artificial intelligence computing capacity

signals.headline: TrendForce sees Meta and AWS shifting more AI server volume to their own ASICs in 2027
signals.whyItMatters: If Meta and AWS move more of their 2027 builds to in-house chips, a bigger capex pie does not mean a proportionally bigger NVIDIA slice.
signals.evidence: significantly accelerating deployment of its proprietary AI ASICs in 2027

signals.headline: Worldwide Server Market Revenue Hits Record $166.3 Billion in the Second Quarter of 2026
signals.whyItMatters: Custom-accelerator servers grew more than eight times as fast as GPU servers and GPU units fell, so NVIDIA's growth is leaning on price while rivals gain volume.
signals.evidence: GPU-accelerated servers generated $87.4 billion (+28.1% YoY); other accelerated servers +237.6% to $27.5 billion; GPU unit shipments fell 10.8%

signals.headline: AI Infrastructure Spending Jumps to $121 Billion in Q2 2026; 2026 Forecast Raised to $521 Billion
signals.whyItMatters: IDC raised its 2026 forecast by $24 billion and expects high pricing to last into late 2027, which supports NVIDIA holding firm on price.
signals.evidence: elevated pricing to persist through at least the second half of 2027

signals.headline: Dell'Oro: Data Center capex grew 92% in 2Q-2026 (caveats galore)
signals.whyItMatters: Spending is still concentrated in NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra, but some of the 92% is memory and storage inflation rather than more racks, so headline capex overstates unit demand.
signals.evidence: supply constraints could limit the pace at which planned infrastructure is deployed

signals.headline: Silicon Data H100 rental index reads $3.08 per GPU-hour, up from $2.89 on October 27
signals.whyItMatters: When rent on older H100s keeps rising, buyers are short of compute, which keeps NVIDIA's newer systems priced firmly.
signals.evidence: $3.08 per GPU-hour as of November 25, 2026

signals.headline: Meta Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results
signals.whyItMatters: Meta narrowed 2026 capex to $135-145 billion but gave no 2027 number, so it is the one big budget the long cannot yet count on.
signals.evidence: still developing our budget and capacity plans for next year

signals.headline: OpenRouter crosses a 10 quadrillion annual token run rate
signals.whyItMatters: Inference usage grew more than sixfold since May, and that usage is what makes the cloud buyers' GPU spending pay back.
signals.evidence: has hit an annualized run rate of over 10 quadrillion tokens

signals.headline: NVIDIA takes on up to $32 billion of conditional obligations tied to AI cloud providers
signals.whyItMatters: Part of the fastest-growing demand is being supported by NVIDIA's own commitments and guarantees, so some orders depend on NVIDIA's balance sheet rather than end-customer budgets.
signals.evidence: up to $32B in conditional obligations tied to AI cloud providers; guarantees up to $118B

signals.headline: NVIDIA raises its fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook to about 75% from 70%
signals.whyItMatters: Fiscal 2028 is mostly calendar 2027, so NVIDIA is telling investors it already sees next year's buyer budgets rising, which is the opposite of the kill test.
signals.evidence: from 70% to about 75%

signals.headline: NVIDIA's AI cloud, industrial and enterprise sales grew 195% to $47.5 billion, against 71% growth for hyperscalers
signals.whyItMatters: Hyperscale customers are now only about 56% of NVIDIA's data center revenue, so a cut by two of the big four would hurt less than the thesis assumes.
signals.evidence: their year-over-year growth rate of 195% exceeded the 71% growth in hyperscale

signals.headline: Microsoft CFO dismisses the AI overcapacity worry but says spending can be reined in if demand changes
signals.whyItMatters: Hood is telling investors the land and building spend is flexible, so Microsoft could slow orders within a quarter or two if Azure demand softens.
signals.evidence: If the demand environment changes, you just slow down

signals.headline: Microsoft lowers its capex outlook because of an accounting change, not a spending slowdown
signals.whyItMatters: Moving data center leases from finance to operating treatment cut the reported capex number by about $15 billion while lease commitments jumped, so a headline capex cut is not proof the kill test has fired.
signals.evidence: Uncommenced lease commitments rose to $329.1 billion from $196.6 billion

signals.headline: AWS will be a $1T business, Jassy says, but first it will spend big
signals.whyItMatters: If AWS really grows above 40% in both 2027 and 2028, Amazon needs more capacity each year, which keeps its share of rack orders rising even as Trainium grows.
signals.evidence: we believe that AWS can grow north of 40% in each 2027 and in 2028

signals.headline: Amazon says Trainium revenue commitments rose more than 20x and it will sell the chip outside AWS late in 2027
signals.whyItMatters: Amazon's 2027 capex can rise without NVIDIA getting a matching share, and from late 2027 Trainium competes for other companies' budgets too.
signals.evidence: intend to do so late in 2027

signals.headline: Google Cloud starts shipping TPU systems and becomes a chipmaker
signals.whyItMatters: Alphabet expects most of its signed TPU system sales to land in 2027, the same year NVIDIA is counting on rising hyperscaler budgets.
signals.evidence: the vast majority of the revenues from these agreements will be realized in 2027

signals.headline: TrendForce 2027 forecast: Google TPU shipments to at least double again, NVIDIA high-end platforms up 30%
signals.whyItMatters: If TPUs at least double while NVIDIA's high-end units grow about 30%, Google's spending growth goes disproportionately to its own chip.
signals.evidence: 預期 2027 年出貨量將持續翻倍以上 (2027 shipments expected to at least double again)

signals.headline: AI Server Outlook: 30% Growth Expected in 2027, but Supply Chain Prospects Diverge
signals.whyItMatters: TrendForce sees custom chip units doubling and passing GPUs in 2027, so rising cloud budgets no longer translate one for one into NVIDIA orders.
signals.evidence: ASIC shipments double and pass GPUs

signals.headline: Meta targets 1H27 deployment for new TSMC-made AI chip, claims efficiency edge over NVIDIA
signals.whyItMatters: Meta is committing over 1 gigawatt of its own chip in 2027 and says a 30% chip cost premium is hard to justify at that scale, which caps NVIDIA's share of its budget.
signals.evidence: roughly 30% increase in chip costs

signals.headline: Analysis: AI investment boom puts Big Tech's free cash flow under pressure
signals.whyItMatters: If the five big spenders add $1.57 of capex for every $1 of new cash flow through 2027, any slip in AI revenue makes a budget cut more likely.
signals.evidence: by roughly $534 billion

signals.headline: Marvell announces conference call to review third quarter of fiscal 2027 results
signals.whyItMatters: Marvell co-designs Trainium and Maia, so its December 1 custom revenue guide is the next dated read on how much 2027 hyperscaler spend skips NVIDIA.
signals.evidence: on Tuesday, December 1, 2026, at 1:30 p.m. Pacific Time

signals.headline: Nvidia tells biggest customers AI server prices will rise more than 15% for systems shipped from early 2027
signals.whyItMatters: A price rise of this size on Rubin and Blackwell systems is the main offset to the 2027 memory bill, and it is why management can promise margins recover to 72-73% next year.
signals.evidence: more than 15%

signals.headline: Kress says Hopper GPUs have recontracted at up to twice their original price
signals.whyItMatters: When three-year-old Hopper capacity reprices at up to double and B300 rental rates are up more than 60%, buyers are short of compute, which is what a supply-limited market looks like.
signals.evidence: Hopper GPUs have recontracted at up to twice their original price under the multi-year agreements.

signals.headline: Nvidia's inventory climbs 86% to $39.7 billion as Vera Rubin production ramps
signals.whyItMatters: Inventory has nearly doubled since January while NVIDIA says it cannot meet demand; if those parts are finished goods waiting on data centers rather than components, the limit is shifting from supply to deployment.
signals.evidence: Inventory climbed 86% to $39.7 billion as the company ramped up production of its Vera Rubin NVL72 rack systems

signals.headline: NVIDIA ramps production and begins shipping Vera Rubin NVL72
signals.whyItMatters: NVIDIA's own account is that Rubin is shipping at volume now, with nearly $20 billion in its first quarter, which undercuts reports that HBM4 has pushed the ramp into 2027.
signals.evidence: the fastest product ramp in the company's history

signals.headline: Industry sources raise HBM4 concerns over NVIDIA Vera Rubin ramp
signals.whyItMatters: If HBM4 really caps Rubin volume into the first half of 2027, that confirms supply is the limit but also slows the shift to the product that is supposed to lift margins back up.
signals.evidence: could push mass production into the first half of 2027, beyond its previous second-half 2026 shipment outlook

signals.headline: SK hynix posts an 80% operating margin and expects HBM4 to overtake HBM3E in the fourth quarter
signals.whyItMatters: NVIDIA's main memory supplier now earns a higher margin than NVIDIA's own 75% gross margin, a sign that the scarce part in each GPU is the memory and that the supplier is setting the price.
signals.evidence: with an operating margin of 80%

signals.headline: Micron guides fiscal first-quarter revenue to $61.5 billion with non-GAAP gross margin near 86%
signals.whyItMatters: A memory maker guiding to an 86% gross margin, more than ten points above NVIDIA's guide, shows how much of the AI server's value has moved to HBM and DRAM.
signals.evidence: approximately 86.25% (non-GAAP)

signals.headline: Micron to report fiscal first-quarter results on December 17, 2026
signals.whyItMatters: Micron's December 17 call is the first supplier report after NVIDIA's guide, and its HBM pricing commentary for 2027 tells you whether the 72-73% fiscal 2028 margin guide still holds.
signals.evidence: Thursday, December 17, 2026, at 2:30 p.m. Mountain time

signals.headline: TSMC reportedly plans up to 10% price hikes in 2027 with extra HPC premiums, Apple and NVIDIA in focus
signals.whyItMatters: On top of a possible 20% CoWoS increase, a 5-10% wafer rise plus a 10-15% surcharge on orders above commitments hits the customer that keeps asking for more than it booked, which is NVIDIA.
signals.evidence: TSMC plans to impose an additional 10% to 15% surcharge on top of the base adjustment.

signals.headline: What Nvidia's B200 AI chip costs to make
signals.whyItMatters: If HBM is about $2,900 and CoWoS about $1,100 of a $6,400 build, memory and packaging are roughly 60% of NVIDIA's chip cost, so the 2027 price rises at SK hynix and TSMC land on most of its cost of goods.
signals.evidence: HBM3E, 192 GB $2,900; CoWoS-L packaging $1,100; Packaging yield loss $1,000; Manufacturing cost ~$6,400

signals.headline: NVIDIA's Vera Rubin rack hit with 435% memory price surge, pushing HBM4 and LPDDR5X bill to $2M of $7.8M total
signals.whyItMatters: Memory went from about 9% of a Grace Blackwell rack to about 26% of a Rubin rack, so each Rubin shipment carries far more supplier cost than the Blackwell it replaces.
signals.evidence: Memory now accounts for 26% of the entire system cost

signals.headline: Morgan Stanley: CoWoS demand to nearly double by 2027, with NVIDIA at about 45% of the total
signals.whyItMatters: Morgan Stanley sees 2027 CoWoS demand up 93% while Goldman sees TSMC capacity up 114%, so packaging may stop being the bottleneck next year and NVIDIA's share of it is falling as AMD and custom chips grow.
signals.evidence: global CoWoS demand will reach 2.694 million wafers in 2027, a 93% increase from 1.394 million wafers in 2026

signals.headline: NVIDIA announces CEO transition as Jensen Huang resigns and Colette Kress becomes interim CEO
signals.whyItMatters: The founder-CEO stepped away for eleven days before the board brought him back on Nov 22, which tested how much of the story rests on one person.
signals.evidence: Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately.

signals.headline: US Senate summons Nvidia's Huang and Lutnick to testify
signals.whyItMatters: A public hearing on December 3 keeps NVIDIA's China sales in front of lawmakers who can push for tighter export law.
signals.evidence: requested that they appear in a public hearing on December 3

signals.headline: Nvidia chip restrictions unlikely in final NDAA as GAIN AI and Chip Security Acts are dropped
signals.whyItMatters: Without the GAIN AI Act there is no US-buyers-first rule in statute, so NVIDIA keeps freedom to sell abroad for at least another year.
signals.evidence: Several proposals aimed at AI chip exports were reportedly excluded from the final NDAA negotiations.

signals.headline: Nvidia H200 chips pile up in Hong Kong as Beijing holds back, Reuters says
signals.whyItMatters: Beijing steering its cloud giants to domestic chips means China demand may not come back even if Washington allows it.
signals.evidence: About 600,000 of Nvidia's H200 AI chips are being stored in Hong Kong.

signals.headline: US moves to block China's remote access to AI chips amid Nvidia scandal
signals.whyItMatters: Licenses are now needed to ship to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, which slows sales to the Southeast Asian clouds that rent compute to Chinese firms.
signals.evidence: Nvidia shares fell 4.1% on Monday and have lost more than 30% of their market value over the past month.

signals.headline: Treasury's Bessent blames Lutnick's Commerce Department for not restricting Nvidia chips to China
signals.whyItMatters: If Megaspeed is blacklisted, a buyer of more than $4 billion of NVIDIA chips goes away and other Southeast Asian customers face closer checks.
signals.evidence: Megaspeed has purchased more than $4 billion worth of Nvidia's advanced semiconductors.
signals.sourceName: Associated Press via Anchorage Daily News

signals.headline: Chip Tariff Phase Two confirmed: build in America or pay, Lutnick announces
signals.whyItMatters: If phase two drops the data center exemption and reaches servers, every rack the hyperscalers import gets more expensive and their budgets buy fewer of them.
signals.evidence: Companies that don't manufacture in the US should expect to pay to enter the greatest market in the world.

signals.headline: Applying semiconductor and server tariffs to data centers would now cost the US about $180 billion a year, CCIA says
signals.whyItMatters: A 25% tariff on chips and servers works out to a 15.6% tax on data center construction, which would come straight out of the capex that drives NVIDIA's demand.
signals.evidence: would put about $900 billion of planned 2027 to 2031 U.S. data center investment at risk

signals.headline: US DOJ examines Nvidia's $12.93 billion Hugging Face acquisition
signals.whyItMatters: The review sits inside a broader look at NVIDIA's conduct, including the Groq deal, and a conduct case could limit the bundling that supports its pricing.
signals.evidence: The review sits inside a broader examination of Nvidia's business practices.

signals.headline: European Commission takes new steps in informal Nvidia antitrust investigation
signals.whyItMatters: The EU probe is still informal, but it is moving toward a case that could make NVIDIA sell GPUs and networking separately in Europe.
signals.evidence: European Commission takes new steps in informal Nvidia antitrust investigation

signals.headline: What we know about China's military exercises around Taiwan
signals.whyItMatters: Roughly 100 ships drilled around Taiwan without a blockade, which shows both how exposed TSMC's supply is and that shipping kept moving.
signals.evidence: We are not going to wake up tomorrow to an operation where Taiwan is being taken by force.

signals.headline: Director Mark Stevens sells 1,356,000 NVIDIA shares at an average of $219.72
signals.whyItMatters: A director cashing out about $298 million two months before the shares fell below $150 is a sign insiders saw the stock as fully priced.
signals.evidence: Shares sold: 1,356,000 at a weighted average price of $219.7219

signals.headline: General Counsel Tim Teter sells 30,000 NVIDIA shares between $146 and $157 under a 10b5-1 plan
signals.whyItMatters: The sale is small and was set up in May, so it says little about conviction, but it shows insiders still selling with the stock near $150.
signals.evidence: effected pursuant to a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan adopted by the Reporting Person on May 22, 2026

signals.headline: AMD reports third quarter 2026 financial results
signals.whyItMatters: AMD's data center revenue nearly doubled on the MI450 launch, and Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle are already running Helios racks, so the same budgets NVIDIA counts on now have a second rack-scale supplier.
signals.evidence: Data Center segment revenue was a record $8.5 billion, up 97% year-over-year

signals.headline: Broadcom predicts AI chip revenue to double in 2027
signals.whyItMatters: Broadcom says it has supply to reach about $115 billion of AI revenue in fiscal 2027, and Anthropic, a major NVIDIA buyer, is set to become its largest custom chip customer, which moves real dollars from GPUs to custom silicon.
signals.evidence: Anthropic is on track to become our largest XPU customer in 2027 and sustain that in 2028.

signals.headline: Broadcom's SC26 Open Ethernet Fabric: AI tail latency vs. proprietary interconnects and Cisco Silicon One
signals.whyItMatters: Broadcom is pitching open Ethernet directly against NVLink and InfiniBand at cluster scale, so if hyperscalers adopt it, NVIDIA's networking revenue per rack is the number that shrinks.
signals.evidence: connect approximately 128,000 accelerators through two switching tiers

signals.headline: Amazon releases an impressive new AI chip and teases an Nvidia-friendly roadmap
signals.whyItMatters: Trainium4 is being built to plug into NVIDIA's NVLink Fusion interconnect, so even Amazon's own chip roadmap keeps NVIDIA networking inside AWS racks rather than designing it out.
signals.evidence: Nvidia's NVLink Fusion high-speed chip interconnect technology

signals.headline: Microsoft to expand Azure Maia system to multi-gigawatt deployments
signals.whyItMatters: Microsoft says Maia 300 will give 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems and will scale to multiple gigawatts from 2027, which takes inference capacity out of Azure's future NVIDIA orders.
signals.evidence: We will scale our Azure Maia family to multi-gigawatt deployments starting in 2027

signals.headline: Marvell Investor Day 2026 targets $80B FY 2031 revenue with custom silicon and optics
signals.whyItMatters: Marvell is planning for custom chip revenue to reach about $30 billion by fiscal 2031, backed by a Google warrant tied to TPU work, which is a forecast that hyperscalers keep shifting spend toward their own silicon.
signals.evidence: on a path to approximately $30 billion by FY 2031

signals.headline: Arista posts record growth as AI networking supercycle accelerates
signals.whyItMatters: Arista's 58.5% growth and more than 100 Etherlink customers show Ethernet AI networking is booming, which grows the market NVIDIA's Spectrum-X sells into but also proves buyers have a strong non-NVIDIA option.
signals.evidence: we are forecasting greater than 10 gigawatts of deployment

signals.headline: Nvidia's China AI chip share falls to 34% as Huawei reaches 28%
signals.whyItMatters: IDC counts NVIDIA's China shipments down 44% in the first half while Huawei shipped 572,000 units, so the China market NVIDIA lost to export rules is being filled by a local rival and may not come back.
signals.evidence: fell to 34% in the first half of 2026

signals.headline: Huawei accelerates AI chip roadmap to 2027 in aggressive push against Nvidia
signals.whyItMatters: Huawei pulled the Ascend 960DT forward to the first quarter of 2027, but it cannot make enough chips for China and only ships trial lots abroad, so it threatens NVIDIA's China business without yet threatening its sales elsewhere.
signals.evidence: local appetite for Ascend chips currently outstrips manufacturing capacity

signals.headline: TSMC posts a sixth straight record profit but turns cautious on 2027
signals.whyItMatters: If TSMC itself says AI demand is well ahead of what it can make, NVIDIA is still selling into a shortage, which keeps its pricing firm.
signals.evidence: demand still far exceeds its supply capacity

signals.headline: After TSMC's 3Q26 earnings: brokerages see CoWoS capacity more than doubling in 2027
signals.whyItMatters: More than doubling CoWoS lets NVIDIA ship more units, but it also erodes the shortage that holds up its pricing and gives custom-chip rivals room to get packaged.
signals.evidence: surging 114% YoY to 2.73 million in 2027 (227,500 monthly)

signals.headline: Micron blew past estimates and says it can't see when the memory shortage ends
signals.whyItMatters: A memory shortage with no end in sight keeps NVIDIA's output capped and its pricing firm, but NVIDIA pays much more for every HBM stack in 2027.
signals.evidence: A large part of the volume is already sold out for 2027… and the prices are much higher than 2026.

signals.headline: Samsung Electronics announces third quarter 2026 results
signals.whyItMatters: Samsung shipping HBM4 at scale gives NVIDIA a real second source next to SK hynix, which means more memory for Rubin and a little more leverage on price.
signals.evidence: significantly scaled up sales of HBM4 on the back of industry-leading product competitiveness

signals.headline: NVIDIA Q3 FY 2027: Vera Rubin gains raise supply commitments
signals.whyItMatters: Locking up years of memory protects NVIDIA's share of a scarce input, but $390 billion of commitments becomes a heavy fixed bill if demand slows.
signals.evidence: supply commitments increased to $390 billion from $279 billion in Q2 FY 2027

signals.headline: NVIDIA Rubin ramp delayed to 2027 on HBM snag
signals.whyItMatters: Low HBM4 yields at the memory suppliers push Rubin's main ramp into next year, so Blackwell has to carry revenue growth for longer.
signals.evidence: Low HBM4 yields constrain chip shipments.

signals.headline: Hon Hai's Q3 net profit hits record high amid AI boom
signals.whyItMatters: Cloud and networking, which is mostly NVIDIA racks, is now more than half of Foxconn's revenue, a sign the racks are being built and shipped as fast as planned.
signals.evidence: cloud and networking division accounted for 54 percent of total revenue in the third quarter

signals.headline: Quanta Computer posts record revenue as AI servers squeeze gross margin to 4.75%
signals.whyItMatters: Quanta expects AI servers to be an even bigger share of its business in 2027, which only happens if the hyperscalers keep ordering NVIDIA racks next year.
signals.evidence: Third-quarter revenue rose 125.2% year-over-year and 7.6% from the second quarter.

signals.headline: NVIDIA expands commitments with supply chain partners to support AI infrastructure buildout
signals.whyItMatters: NVIDIA is paying to build packaging capacity outside TSMC, which lifts its shipment ceiling and makes it less dependent on one packaging supplier.
signals.evidence: multiyear agreement supported by multibillion-dollar funding from NVIDIA

signals.headline: NVIDIA expands commitments with supply chain partners, including Amkor in Arizona and South Korea
signals.whyItMatters: Amkor capacity in Arizona and Korea moves some of NVIDIA's packaging out of Taiwan, which cuts the geographic risk sitting under every GPU.
signals.evidence: Our agreements with NVIDIA support investments in Arizona and South Korea.

signals.headline: NVIDIA taps six suppliers to expand AI chip substrate, packaging and testing capacity
signals.whyItMatters: IBIDEN tripling its Ono plant eases the substrate limit, but the new capacity only starts in 2028, so substrates stay a cap on NVIDIA's volumes through 2027.
signals.evidence: targets three times its current capacity

signals.headline: NVIDIA taps six suppliers to expand AI chip substrate, packaging and testing capacity
signals.whyItMatters: NVIDIA prepaying for US test capacity keeps testing from becoming the next bottleneck and adds a US step to a chain that runs mostly through Taiwan.
signals.evidence: NVIDIA is providing a $1.1 billion capacity reservation advance to KYEC for new U.S. testing facilities

signals.headline: TSMC reportedly eyes 20% CoWoS price hike, skips equipment price renegotiations amid AI demand surge
signals.whyItMatters: A packaging price hike proves CoWoS is still the bottleneck, which supports the supply-limited thesis, but it also lands on NVIDIA's cost of goods.
signals.evidence: the foundry giant is reportedly weighing price hikes of up to 20%, with some packaging lead times already stretching

signals.headline: Report: TSMC to double CoWoS capacity by 2028 as AI chip shortage spills over to rivals
signals.whyItMatters: Doubling CoWoS lets NVIDIA ship far more units, but once packaging stops being scarce the pricing support in the supply-limit thesis weakens.
signals.evidence: CoWoS capacity to sit at 260,000 wafers per month by the end of 2028, up from 130,000 at the end of this year

signals.headline: SK hynix reportedly plans new HBM4 equipment orders, with P&T6 in focus despite NVIDIA uncertainty
signals.whyItMatters: SK hynix is adding HBM capacity with Google's TPU in view, so new memory supply is not reserved for NVIDIA and helps custom chips scale.
signals.evidence: P&T6 at full capacity could lift HBM output by more than 20,000 wafers per month; TPU shipments projected to nearly double from 8-9 million units in 2027 to 16-18 million in 2029

signals.headline: Samsung's HBM prices tipped to more than double in 2027
signals.whyItMatters: If blended HBM prices rise 121% next year, the memory bill per Rubin rack climbs sharply and pushes NVIDIA's margin toward the 70% kill line.
signals.evidence: TrendForce forecasts that the global HBM market's blended average selling price will rise 121 percent year-on-year in 2027

signals.headline: Samsung Electronics passes Nvidia quality tests for next-generation HBM4E memory chips
signals.whyItMatters: A qualified second source for HBM4E gives NVIDIA more volume for Rubin Ultra and some leverage against SK hynix on price.
signals.evidence: Samsung's 12-layer HBM4E product reportedly passed qualification tests by Nvidia and major hyperscale customers at the end of September

signals.headline: Hon Hai's Q3 net profit hits record high amid AI boom
signals.whyItMatters: Foxconn's AI racks grew faster than it expected last quarter, so NVIDIA systems are clearing the assembly line at the pace its data center guide needs.
signals.evidence: Net profit NT$77.52 billion, up 34% year on year; AI servers and AI racks grew more than expected in the third quarter

signals.headline: NVIDIA expands commitments with supply chain partners to support AI infrastructure buildout
signals.whyItMatters: NVIDIA is paying to remove the substrate bottleneck, which protects its 2027 and 2028 unit growth even if T-glass and ABF stay tight industry-wide.
signals.evidence: Kinsus plans to expand its ABF substrate capacity dedicated to NVIDIA by more than 3.5x; added capacity targeted for Q3 2028

signals.headline: Google reportedly books Intel for packaging more than 3 million TPUs in 2028
signals.whyItMatters: A cheaper packaging route outside TSMC removes the CoWoS queue that has held back Google's TPU, the custom chip most likely to take NVIDIA share.
signals.evidence: Bernstein estimates EMIB costs a few hundred dollars per chip, versus $900 to $1,000 for CoWoS on a Rubin-class processor

signals.headline: America's grid upgrade hinges on a 400-ton machine designed in the 1800s, and just one U.S. mill makes the special steel inside it
signals.whyItMatters: When transformers take over three years and gas turbines up to seven, customers can have the capex budget but no powered building to put NVIDIA racks in.
signals.evidence: Ordering a large power transformer can take more than three years; gas turbine delivery times have stretched to between three and seven years
